Kabzeel@Jos.15.21-1Ch.description: Kabzeel, a town in the Negev, was the hometown of Benaiah, one of David's mighty men (<ref="Joshua 15:21; 2Sa.23.20; 1Ch.11.22">Joshua 15:21; 2Sa.23.20; 1Ch.11.22</ref>).
Kabzeel@Jos.15.21-1Ch.name: Kabzeel

Kadesh@Gen.14.7-Psa.description: Kadesh (Kadesh-barnea, En-mishpat), an important oasis in the Wilderness of Zin, was a key location during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings.
Kadesh@Gen.14.7-Psa.name: Kadesh

Kadmiel@Ezr.2.40-Neh.description: Kadmiel was a Levite who returned from Babylonian exile and played a significant role in the rebuilding of the temple and the spiritual renewal of the people.
Kadmiel@Ezr.2.40-Neh.name: Kadmiel

Kadmonites@Gen.15.19.description: The Kadmonites were one of the Canaanite people groups living in the land promised to Abraham's descendants.
Kadmonites@Gen.15.19.name: Kadmonites

Kain@Num.24.22-Jos.description: Kain, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:57">Joshua 15:57</ref>), is possibly associated with the Kenites mentioned in <ref="Numbers 24:22">Numbers 24:22</ref>.
Kain@Num.24.22-Jos.name: Kain

Kallai@Neh.12.20.description: Kallai was a priest who served during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua, after the Babylonian exile.
Kallai@Neh.12.20.name: Kallai

Kamon@Jdg.10.5.description: Kamon, a city in Gilead where Jair, a judge of Israel, was buried (<ref="Judges 10:5">Judges 10:5</ref>).
Kamon@Jdg.10.5.name: Kamon

Kanah@Jos.16.8-.description: The Brook of Kanah formed part of the border between the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh (<ref="Joshua 16:8; 17:9">Joshua 16:8; 17:9</ref>).
Kanah@Jos.16.8-.name: Kanah

Kanah@Jos.19.28-Jhn.description: Kanah was a border town in Asher's territory, while Cana was the village in Galilee where Jesus performed his first miracle.
Kanah@Jos.19.28-Jhn.name: Kanah

Kareah@2Ki.25.23-Jer.description: Kareah was the father of Johanan and Jonathan, two military leaders who joined Gedaliah after the fall of Jerusalem to the Babylonians.
Kareah@2Ki.25.23-Jer.name: Kareah

Karka@Jos.15.3.description: Karka, a location along the southern border of the tribe of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:3">Joshua 15:3</ref>).
Karka@Jos.15.3.name: Karka

Karkor@Jdg.8.10.description: Karkor, the place where Gideon defeated the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna (<ref="Judges 8:10">Judges 8:10</ref>).
Karkor@Jdg.8.10.name: Karkor

Kartan@Jos.21.32.description: Kartan, a city given to the Levites within the territory of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 21:32">Joshua 21:32</ref>).
Kartan@Jos.21.32.name: Kartan

Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk.description: Kedar was a son of Ishmael and the eponymous ancestor of a nomadic Arab tribe known for their tents and flocks.
Kedar@Gen.25.13-Ezk.name: Kedar

Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch.description: Kedemah was a son of Ishmael, while the Nodab were a Hagrite tribe defeated by the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh.
Kedemah@Gen.25.15-1Ch.name: Kedemah

Kedemoth@Deu.2.26-1Ch.description: Kedemoth, a town in Moab from which Moses sent messengers to Sihon, later became a Levitical city within the territory of Reuben (<ref="Deu.2.26; Joshua 13:18; 21:37; 1Ch.6.79">Deu.2.26; Joshua 13:18; 21:37; 1Ch.6.79</ref>).
Kedemoth@Deu.2.26-1Ch.name: Kedemoth

Kedesh@Jos.12.22-1Ch.description: Kedesh (Kedesh-naphtali), a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua, became a Levitical city and a city of refuge in the territory of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 12:22; 19:37; 20:7; 21:32">Joshua 12:22; 19:37; 20:7; 21:32</ref>).
Kedesh@Jos.12.22-1Ch.name: Kedesh

Kehelathah@Num.33.22-.description: Kehelathah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings after leaving Mount Sinai (<ref="Numbers 33:22-23">Numbers 33:22-23</ref>).
Kehelathah@Num.33.22-.name: Kehelathah

Keilah@Jos.15.44-Neh.description: Keilah, a town in the Shephelah of Judah, was rescued by David from Philistine attack but later threatened to betray him to Saul (<ref="Joshua 15:44; 1Samuel 23">Joshua 15:44; 1Samuel 23</ref>).
Keilah@Jos.15.44-Neh.name: Keilah

Kelaiah@Ezr.10.23.description: Kelaiah, also known as Kelita, was a Levite who had married a foreign woman and pledged to put her away during Ezra's reform.
Kelaiah@Ezr.10.23.name: Kelaiah

Kelita@Neh.8.7-.description: Kelita was a Levite who helped explain the Law to the people and sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.
Kelita@Neh.8.7-.name: Kelita

Kemuel@1Ch.27.17.description: Kemuel, the son of Hebron, was the leader of the Levites during the reign of King David.
Kemuel@1Ch.27.17.name: Kemuel

Kemuel@Gen.22.21.description: Kemuel was a son of Nahor and Milcah and the father of Aram.
Kemuel@Gen.22.21.name: Kemuel

Kemuel@Num.34.24.description: Kemuel, the son of Shiphtan, was a leader from the tribe of Ephraim appointed to help divide the Promised Land.
Kemuel@Num.34.24.name: Kemuel

Kenan@Gen.5.9-Luk.description: Kenan (Cainan), the son of Enosh, was a descendant of Seth and an ancestor of Noah.
Kenan@Gen.5.9-Luk.name: Kenan

Kenath@Num.21.30-1Ch.description: Kenath, a city in Gilead captured by Nobah and renamed after himself, was later recaptured by Geshur and Aram (<ref="Numbers 32:42; Judges 8:11; 1Ch.2.23">Numbers 32:42; Judges 8:11; 1Ch.2.23</ref>).
Kenath@Num.21.30-1Ch.name: Kenath

Kenaz@1Ch.4.15.description: Kenaz was a descendant of Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
Kenaz@1Ch.4.15.name: Kenaz

Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch.description: Kenaz was one of the clans of Edom, descended from Esau through his son Eliphaz.
Kenaz@Gen.36.11-1Ch.name: Kenaz

Kenaz@Num.32.12-1Ch.description: Kenaz was the father of Othniel, a judge of Israel who delivered the Israelites from the oppression of Cushan-rishathaim.
Kenaz@Num.32.12-1Ch.name: Kenaz

Kenites@Gen.15.19-1Ch.description: The Kenites were a nomadic tribe who lived in the region of Canaan and were generally friendly to the Israelites, often providing them with assistance and support.
Kenites@Gen.15.19-1Ch.name: Kenites

Kenizzites@Gen.15.19.description: The Kenizzites were one of the Canaanite tribes inhabiting the land God promised to give to Abraham's descendants.
Kenizzites@Gen.15.19.name: Kenizzites

Keren-happuch@Job.42.14.description: Keren-happuch was the name of Job's third daughter, born to him after God restored his fortunes.
Keren-happuch@Job.42.14.name: Keren-happuch

Kerioth-hezron@Jos.15.25.description: Kerioth-hezron, also known as Hazor, was a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:25">Joshua 15:25</ref>).
Kerioth-hezron@Jos.15.25.name: Kerioth-hezron

Keros@Ezr.2.44-Neh.description: Keros was the name of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
Keros@Ezr.2.44-Neh.name: Keros

Keturah@Gen.25.1-1Ch.description: Keturah was the concubine Abraham took after the death of Sarah, and she bore him six sons.
Keturah@Gen.25.1-1Ch.name: Keturah

Keziah@Job.42.14.description: Keziah was the name of Job's second daughter, born to him after God restored his fortunes.
Keziah@Job.42.14.name: Keziah

Kibroth-hattaavah@Num.11.34-Deu.description: Kibroth-hattaavah, meaning "graves of craving," was a place where the Israelites complained about the lack of meat and were punished with a plague (<ref="Numbers 11:34-35; 33:16-17; Deu.9.22">Numbers 11:34-35; 33:16-17; Deu.9.22</ref>).
Kibroth-hattaavah@Num.11.34-Deu.name: Kibroth-hattaavah

Kibzaim@Jos.21.22-1Ch.description: Kibzaim, also known as Jokmeam, was a Levitical city within the territory of Ephraim (<ref="Joshua 21:22; 1Ch.6.68">Joshua 21:22; 1Ch.6.68</ref>).
Kibzaim@Jos.21.22-1Ch.name: Kibzaim

Kidron@2Sa.15.23-Jhn.description: The Kidron Valley, also known as the Valley of Jehoshaphat, is located east of Jerusalem and was the site of several significant events in the Bible.
Kidron@2Sa.15.23-Jhn.name: Kidron

Kinah@Jos.15.22.description: Kinah, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:22">Joshua 15:22</ref>).
Kinah@Jos.15.22.name: Kinah

King's_Highway@Num.20.17-.description: The King's Highway, an ancient trade route through Edom and Moab, was the path the Israelites sought to use during their journey to Canaan (<ref="Numbers 20:17; 21:22">Numbers 20:17; 21:22</ref>).
King's_Highway@Num.20.17-.name: King's_Highway

King's_Valley@Gen.14.17-2Sa.description: The King's Valley, located near Salem (Jerusalem), was the site where Melchizedek met Abraham and where Absalom erected a pillar for himself (<ref="Genesis 14:17; 2Sa.18.18">Genesis 14:17; 2Sa.18.18</ref>).
King's_Valley@Gen.14.17-2Sa.name: King's_Valley

Kir@1Sa.22.3-Jer.description: Kir, also known as Mizpeh, was a Moabite city that faced destruction by the Babylonians (<ref="Isaiah 15:1; Jeremiah 48:1">Isaiah 15:1; Jeremiah 48:1, 23</ref>).
Kir@1Sa.22.3-Jer.name: Kir

Kir@2Ki.16.9-Amo.description: Kir, a city or region in Mesopotamia, possibly Elam, was the place where the Arameans were exiled and from where they originally came (<ref="2Ki.16.9; Amo.9.7">2Ki.16.9; Amo.9.7</ref>).
Kir@2Ki.16.9-Amo.name: Kir

Kiriath-huzoth@Num.22.39.description: Kiriath-huzoth, a place where Balak took Balaam (<ref="Numbers 22:39">Numbers 22:39</ref>).
Kiriath-huzoth@Num.22.39.name: Kiriath-huzoth

Kiriath-jearim@Jos.9.17-Jer.description: Kiriath-jearim, a city where the ark of the covenant resided for 20 years (<ref="1Sa.7.1-2">1Sa.7.1-2</ref>).
Kiriath-jearim@Jos.9.17-Jer.name: Kiriath-jearim

Kiriathaim@1Ch.6.76.description: Kiriathaim, a Levitical city in the territory of Reuben (<ref="1Ch.6.76">1Ch.6.76</ref>).
Kiriathaim@1Ch.6.76.name: Kiriathaim

Kiriathaim@Gen.14.5-Amo.description: Kiriathaim, also known as Kerioth, was a Moabite city later allotted to the tribe of Reuben (<ref="Numbers 32:37; Joshua 13:19; Jeremiah 48:1">Numbers 32:37; Joshua 13:19; Jeremiah 48:1, 23</ref>).
Kiriathaim@Gen.14.5-Amo.name: Kiriathaim

Kish@1Ch.23.21-.description: Kish was a Levite from the clan of Merari, whose descendants were assigned duties in the tabernacle service.
Kish@1Ch.23.21-.name: Kish

Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act.description: Kish was a Benjamite, the father of Saul, who was anointed by Samuel as the first king of Israel.
Kish@1Sa.9.1-Act.name: Kish

Kish@2Ch.29.12.description: Kish, a Levite from the clan of Merari, participated in the purification of the temple during the reign of King Hezekiah.
Kish@2Ch.29.12.name: Kish

Kish@Est.2.5.description: Kish, a Benjamite, was an ancestor of Mordecai, the cousin and guardian of Queen Esther.
Kish@Est.2.5.name: Kish

Kishi@1Ch.6.44-.description: Kishi, also known as Kushaiah, was a Levite from the clan of Merari and the father of Jeduthun (or 'Ethan'), a prominent musician in King David's court.
Kishi@1Ch.6.44-.name: Kishi

Kishion@Jos.19.20-1Ch.description: Kishion (Kedesh), a Levitical city in the territory of Issachar (<ref="Joshua 19:20, 21:28; 1Ch.6.72">Joshua 19:20, 21:28; 1Ch.6.72</ref>).
Kishion@Jos.19.20-1Ch.name: Kishion

Kishon@Jdg.4.7-Psa.description: Kishon, a river in northern Israel, where Deborah and Barak defeated Sisera's army (<ref="Judges 4:7, 13; 5:21">Judges 4:7, 13; 5:21</ref>).
Kishon@Jdg.4.7-Psa.name: Kishon

Kitron@Jos.19.15-Jdg.description: Kitron (Kartah or Kattath), a city in Zebulun that was not conquered by the tribe (<ref="Judges 1:30; Joshua 21:34, 19:15">Judges 1:30; Joshua 21:34, 19:15</ref>).
Kitron@Jos.19.15-Jdg.name: Kitron

Kittim@Gen.10.4-1Ch.description: Kittim, a descendant of Japheth, son of Noah.
Kittim@Gen.10.4-1Ch.name: Kittim

Kiyyun@Amo.5.26.description: Kiyyun was an astral deity that the Israelites worshiped, leading to God's judgment and their exile.
Kiyyun@Amo.5.26.name: Kiyyun

Koa@Ezk.23.23.description: Koa, a people group mentioned by Ezekiel (<ref="Ezk.23.23">Ezk.23.23</ref>).
Koa@Ezk.23.23.name: Koa

Kohath@Gen.46.11-2Ch.description: Kohath, son of Levi, was the ancestor of Moses and Aaron.
Kohath@Gen.46.11-2Ch.name: Kohath

Kolaiah@Jer.29.21.description: Kolaiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
Kolaiah@Jer.29.21.name: Kolaiah

Kolaiah@Neh.11.7.description: Kolaiah, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem.
Kolaiah@Neh.11.7.name: Kolaiah

Korah@1Ch.2.43.description: Korah, son of Hebron, from the tribe of Judah.
Korah@1Ch.2.43.name: Korah

Korah@Exo.6.21-Jud.description: Korah, a Levite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron; his descendants became temple musicians and gatekeepers.
Korah@Exo.6.21-Jud.name: Korah

Korah@Gen.36.16.description: Korah, an Edomite chief, descendant of Eliphaz, son of Esau.
Korah@Gen.36.16.name: Korah

Korah@Gen.36.5-1Ch.description: Korah, son of Esau and Oholibamah
Korah@Gen.36.5-1Ch.name: Korah

Kore@1Ch.9.19-.description: Kore, a Levite gatekeeper, descendant of Korah
Kore@1Ch.9.19-.name: Kore

Kore@2Ch.31.14.description: Kore, a Levite in charge of distributing freewill offerings during Hezekiah's reign.
Kore@2Ch.31.14.name: Kore

Koz@1Ch.4.8.description: Koz, a descendant of Judah through Ashhur.
Koz@1Ch.4.8.name: Koz

Kue@1Ki.10.28-2Ch.description: Kue, a place from which Solomon obtained horses (<ref="1Ki.10.28; 2Ch.1.16">1Ki.10.28; 2Ch.1.16</ref>).
Kue@1Ki.10.28-2Ch.name: Kue
